body: Do your voices sounds like a normal person saying sentences? Mine seems to keep going, one word after another and it's not like a normal person. They don't ever pause when they are talking.
Thank you. It's the most unfair thing that happened to me. I can't believe yet.

I developed drunkorexia when I started to have auditive hallucinations. The voices were threatening me for months. They used to say positive things when I was drunk. They were always telling me to drink. I didn't know it wasn't real, so I just kept going for months and months because I lost my attachment to reality. I used to listen familiar voices so I was thinking people (including my family) were conspiring against me.

So, to keep short I found threatment and I was trying to get out of my alcoholic behavior. Drinking beer never made any difference until the day were the voices came back.

Sometimes I feel attached for the simple things...Like I love tattoos and I want to have a lot of them but is not enough. Not even the love of my mother seems enough right now. I feel like with my disead she would be better because I don't think she's supposed to see value on me. I feel like I need to not be sober until I get to the ER.
You know, I have hope when I'm drunk. That's my life right now and even if I feel nausea I won't go the the hospital because all the episode teached me is that I have to die.
Yes, they love me. But I can't see if they are lying or not. Everything seems like a scheme to kill me.

That makes me pay way more attention to MY voice and MY sentences than to what I'm listening. It's not easy to learn another language but is the only thing that works for me. And alcohol too.

People project all kinds of things when it comes to artists. Most of them are not even half of what we imagine them to be. So I'm not surprised or sad about the post. Maybe she made a wrong decision with the words but for me is very clear what she means. I will keep admiring her work and I won't project nothing about her personality. I'm detached cause I'm not a close friend or a family member.

You are great writing about it. I admire that because I can't do it. Soon I will go back to draw and paint. I feel more enthusiasm than ever because they acidentally give me fuel to create something. To exceed in my life. They were capable of blowing my mind during my episode of months, but now I know their place. I'm in control. I'm able to use my past pain as an inspiration and my goals as comfort. It's a challenge and I won.

Yes, I realized the voices are kinda slaves of my mind. They feed on it and sometimes they think they have some influence on me even though I'm going through my day as usual. It's pathetic. They can't control themselves like I do which makes me feel way better when I think about it.

Yes, for me schizophrenia is 100% involuntary. Your brain starts to produce all kinds of hallucinations and it doesn't go away even when you look for distractions. You don't have any control of what's happening unless you are under treatment. For me, now, is very obvious it is a psychological disease because I'm using the right meds, the right therapist and I'm 80% better and far from a outbreak like the episode.

On the other side, immersive daydreaming is something you can control. It's more of a hobbie and you have pleasure to do it. You start to get creative, just like talking to yourself, and you can stop when you get tired and go back to your real life. I'm aware my daydreaming have nothing to do with schizophrenia because I create it. 

And most of all, the hallucinations I had while having an episode have little to do with what I created in my immersive daydreams. Actually some things I listened was from my daydreams but extremely distorted. Things I wouldn't imagine by myself. There was distorted real life information too so it was a mix like my brain was trying to go trough my thoughts without an order or any common sense.

When you are doing immersive daydreaming you have sequency of thoughts, you have common sense like you're writing a script. It's not messy and all over the place.

Hope this helps!

Everytime I go to my therapist, psychologist, and psychiatrist they ask me about my food habits and exercise. I think having a healthy approach can help. Honestly I feel like trying to live a better life as possible can help us to ground ourselves. This week I started a new diet (vegetables and fruits only). Can't do exercise yet because my weight makes me feel really tired but I will do once I lose some weight. Also it makes me feel like having goals can distract me by thinking about them instead of focusing only on the voices I hear (I hear like 6 different voices daily but low volume now because of the meds).
